title: Name the signal — hand hygiene
brief:
Your ward launched a hand-hygiene campaign after week 8. The chart shows weekly hand-hygiene compliance (%) over 16 weeks, with the median drawn as a dashed line.

Apply the four run-chart signals and name the one you see.

task.stem: Which run-chart signal does this chart show?

options.label: A shift — a run of six or more points on one side of the median.
A trend — five or more points all climbing or all falling.
An astronomical point — one point strikingly different from the rest.

debrief.correct: Yes — a **shift**. From week 9 onward, eight consecutive points sit above the median (67%), well past the threshold of six. The single jump between week 8 and week 9 is not a trend (a trend needs five consecutive steps in one direction), and no point is astronomically far from the rest. A shift up in a 'good' measure like compliance is improvement — and it is holding.
debrief.wrong: Count the points on one side of the median. From week 9, eight weeks in a row sit above the median (67%) — that is a **shift** (six or more consecutive on one side). It is not a trend (no run of five consecutive *steps* up or down) and there is no single astronomical outlier.
debrief.rule_cited: Shift rule — Provost & Murray (2nd ed.), IHI QI 104.
